lands.name: SOC 2
lands.what: An examination by a licensed, independent CPA of a service organization’s controls against the Trust Services Criteria: security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy. It ends in a report, and customers are the ones who ask for it.
lands.lands: It lands on Layer 5: independent evidence that controls exist and work. FedRAMP’s Class A rules accept a SOC 2 Type II from the past 12 months as a way in.

source.title: AICPA Proposes Update of SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria

verification.note: Read on 14 November 2026: ‘SOC 2® is an examination performed by a licensed, independent CPA under the AICPA Attestation Standards’. The criteria in force are the 2017 Trust Services Criteria with the revised points of focus of 2022; a proposed 2027 edition is out for comment until 15 January 2027. The FedRAMP rule is FRC-CLA-ASF in the Consolidated Rules for 2026, read the same day.

lands.name: HIPAA Security Rule
lands.what: Federal regulation, 45 CFR Part 160 and Subparts A and C of Part 164. It binds covered entities and business associates to administrative, physical and technical safeguards for electronic protected health information. A 2025 proposal to strengthen it is still pending.
lands.lands: It lands on Layer 4 as requirements, with a regulator in place of an assessor. CSF 2.0 names it as an example of the legal requirements an organization must track, under GV.OC-03.

source.title: 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C: Security Standards for the Protection of Electronic Protected Health Information

verification.note: Read on 14 November 2026: sections 164.308, 164.310 and 164.312 are the administrative, physical and technical safeguards, and ‘A covered entity or business associate must comply’. The proposed rule of 6 January 2025 (90 FR 898) was still pending: the 2026 Unified Agenda lists it under Long-Term Actions with final action in July 2027.

lands.name: PCI DSS
lands.what: The payment card industry’s data security standard, version 4.0.1: 12 requirements under 6 goals for anyone who stores, processes or transmits cardholder data. It is validated by an assessor’s Report on Compliance or by a Self-Assessment Questionnaire.
lands.lands: It spans Layers 4 and 5 in one document: its own requirements and its own validation, enforced by the card brands and acquirers. NIST’s CSF 2.0 Reference Tool lists PCI DSS among its informative references.

verification.note: Read on 14 November 2026. Version 4.0.1, announced on 11 June 2024, has been the only active version since 1 January 2025 and was still current; the council took comments on it from 3 June to 20 July 2026 toward the next iteration. Only counts are shown here, not the standard’s text.
